title: Solving the Rational Inequality 3/(x - 1) < 2/(x + 1) Graphically and Algebraically
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: (a) Compare the graphs of f(x) = 3/(x - 1) and g(x) = 2/(x + 1) to identify the values of x for which 3/(x - 1) < 2/(x + 1). (b) Confirm the solution set algebraically.

steps.title: Move All Terms to One Side
steps.explanation: Geometrically, the inequality holds where the hyperbola f(x) = 3/(x - 1) lies strictly below g(x) = 2/(x + 1). Algebraically, subtract 2/(x + 1) from both sides.
steps.why: Bringing all terms to one side avoids multiplying by (x - 1)(x + 1), whose sign depends on x.

steps.title: Combine Over a Common Denominator and Simplify
steps.explanation: Combine the fractions over (x - 1)(x + 1) and simplify the numerator: 3x + 3 - 2x + 2 = x + 5. The critical points are x = -5 (zero) and x = -1, 1 (vertical asymptotes).
steps.why: A rational expression can change sign only at the zeros of its numerator and denominator.

steps.title: Conduct Sign Chart Analysis
steps.why: Selecting the intervals where the quotient is strictly negative yields the exact solution set (-inf, -5) U (-1, 1).
